for word into another block of skill prose nor quoted by a row of an inventory in a spec the PR adds under the spec docs path. It proves coverage, never correctness: whether a row's claim is true stays with review and the holdout.

```markdown
## Rule inventory

| Prose rule | Command behaviour | Covering test | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Fail closed on an unreadable ledger, never a pass` | exit 2 on a read error | test/run-open.test.mjs: "unreadable ledger exits 2" | kept |
| `Tick the heartbeat before and after the ladder` | the command ticks it | — | changed: the command ticks it itself |
| `Log the round to graft.md as well` | none | — | dropped: the round record replaces it |
```

- **Section.** Any line starting `## Rule inventory` (a suffix such as `(slice A)` is fine). It runs to the next `## ` heading. Every table in it whose header has a `Prose rule` and a `Disposition` column is read; columns are found by name, case-insensitively, a qualifier after the name is allowed, and other columns are free. A header with one of the two and not the other is an error.
- **Prose rule.** The first code span in the cell is the anchor. Quote the lines the PR deletes, not the block as it stood: when only part of a paragraph goes, the anchor must sit inside the deleted part. Matching ignores `*` and backticks and collapses whitespace, so quote with or without bold leads and code spans. An anchor shorter than 20 characters only covers a deleted block whose whole text it equals. An anchor containing a backtick uses a longer delimiter (``` `` like `this` `` ```); a literal pipe inside a cell is written `\|`.
- **Covering test.** Zero or more `test/<path>.test.mjs` entries, each optionally followed by `: "<test name>"`, separated by `;` or `,`. Each file must exist, and a named test must appear in it as written. A `kept` row needs at least one, so a table with a `kept` row needs this column.
- **Disposition.** Exactly one of `kept`, `changed: <reason>` or `dropped: <reason>`; a reason is required.

What needs no row: text that still appears verbatim in one block of skill prose (a move, a rename, a reflow, a rule extended in place), table separator rows, letterless lines, and a heading or table header row deleted together with every line of its section or table, with nothing added in its place and none of that content reappearing elsewhere. A heading over an empty section is never exempt. A reworded rule needs a row, typically `changed: reworded, same rule`; prose moved to `docs/` needs one too, normally `dropped: moved to docs/<file>`.

Scope follows the artifacts graft commits. The check applies when the PR adds a spec under the spec docs path; a PR that adds or modifies a path under `.faff/anchors/` but commits no spec fails; a PR with neither (a hand-written prose edit) is skipped with a notice. The `--summary` table on the check page lists every row-covered block, `dropped` and `changed` first, for the reviewer.

## Eval coverage — born with the ticket

A judgement seam ships with its eval coverage; the net never plays catch-up (the FAFF-145 / ADR-0004 lesson — every seam used to ship first and the evals chased).

- **Declare the seam.** Every slot skill carries a `judgement_seam:` frontmatter key (sibling to `name` / `user-invocable`): a comma list of the grader `KIND`(s) its LLM-judgement seam owns — or `none` for an asserted-deterministic skill. An alternate occupant declares its slot sibling's KIND(s) (the slot-sibling relaxation), not `none`.
- **Register the coverage in the same change.** A ticket that introduces or changes a judgement seam registers a grader `KIND` + ≥1 case fixture (`eval/cases/<kind>-NNN.json`) + the `eval/seam-registry.json` row — all autonomous-doable. It must **not** require a recorded baseline value: accepting the baseline is the one human-supervised, CI-excluded step (ADR-0004), so the gate would otherwise block every autonomous build.
- **The mechanical backstop.** `faff validate-adapters` gates the structural half: a registry **surface** with no `judgement_seam:` declaration fails (C1); a `covered` KIND with zero cases fails (C2); a `designed` KIND with zero cases and an unrowed slot-skill are loud advisories that flip to a hard fail the instant a row is registered. "Did the ticket actually need a seam" stays review judgement — intent isn't statically inferable.

## For new slot skills

`faffter-dark-authoring-adaptors` scaffolds new adaptors/producers/methodologies **to** this charter — write to it from the start rather than retrofitting.

<!-- Target ADR producer -->
---
name: faffter-noon-adr
description: "Default adr producer: author a settled architecture decision from spec rationale and the ADR log, using the committed adr.md template or Nygard format."
user-invocable: false
judgement_seam: adr-gloss
---

# faffter-noon-adr

The default producer for the **`adr` slot**. Given a *settled* (already-`Chosen`) decision, it authors the ADR body that faff-graft drops into the `faff adr new` scaffold and commits on the feature branch (the `faff adr new` mechanics own the scaffold, numbering, and validate; this producer owns only the prose) — against the repo's **resolved section list**: Nygard (Context / Decision / Consequences) by default, or a committed `adr.md` template's own headings when the repo carries one.

It is the judgement layer over the `faff adr new` deterministic ADR machinery, and the **single ADR-authoring producer**: the generative architecture proposer *decides* architecture and feeds settled decisions into this same slot rather than carrying its own writer.

This is a producer doing-skill, invoked as a configured slot — not a user `/` command. Swap it (`slots.adr`) to change how ADR bodies are authored.

## When it runs

faff-graft **Step 4b**, once a promoted decision is settled and the build is complete. Authoring at *graft* (not the spec stage) is deliberate: the implementation is done, so the *Consequences* are real rather than guess
